clue.text: Dramatist to brandish weapon as reported

indicators.note: as reported says the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read as spelt

parts.note: to brandish is to shake and a spear is a weapon, so the phrase is shake spear

explanation.surface: A playwright is said to have waved a weapon about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as reported' is the homophone signal: SHAKE SPEAR, said aloud, is the name of the playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: William Shakespeare is the most famous English playwright, so he is a dramatist.

clue.text: Grab some grains first for use on cushion

indicators.note: first says the grains piece goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: sand is a mass of small grains
to bag something is to grab or seize it

explanation.surface: Someone snatches a handful of seed to use for a pillow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' reorders the pieces, since the grab word comes first in the clue. The cushion sense is an engraver's: a sand-filled leather pad that supports the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraver's sandbag is a round leather cushion filled with sand, used to support the plate while working.

clue.text: Knight takes very long time embracing lady

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the time word wraps round the knight

parts.note: ages means a very long time, as in waiting for ages
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight spends years courting a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts N inside AGES; 'takes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's first name, borne for example by the early Christian martyr Saint Agnes.

clue.text: More, almost 99, with eight more, say, to disentangle

indicators.note: almost says the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: extra means more, as in extra time
IC is a crossword way of writing ninety-nine in Roman numerals, one before a hundred

indicators.note: say signals that the number is heard, giving a spelling that sounds the same

parts.note: the number eight, spoken

explanation.surface: Adding up ninety-nine and eight more to free oneself from a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims EXTRA to EXTR; 'say' makes EIGHT into ATE, which sounds the same. IC for 99 is a crossword licence; strictly Romans wrote XCIX.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free something from a tangle or difficulty, to release it.

clue.text: Bard found film on river

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the film comes after the river

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
E.T. is the 1982 Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A writer is discovered making a film on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means placed after, so the film goes after the river; 'found' is just a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bard is a literary word for a writer of verse.

clue.text: Performed each dive acrobatically

indicators.note: acrobatically means with tumbling and twisting, so these letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A diver completes every dive with gymnastic flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acrobatically' tells you to rearrange EACH DIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have achieved something is to have carried it out or accomplished it.

clue.text: Taken in by consumers

parts.note: taken in reads like fooled or deceived, but food taken in by those who consume it has been swallowed

explanation.surface: Shoppers are fooled by a sales trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' looks like 'deceived', and consumers look like shoppers; read literally, it is food swallowed by diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been swallowed by diners is food that has been consumed.

clue.text: Plant developed in slum, say

indicators.note: developed suggests property being rebuilt, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A flower grows in a run-down area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges SLUM SAY; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alyssum is a low-growing garden flower of the cabbage family, often with small white or yellow blooms.

clue.text: Heathen admits to being a procrastinator

definitions.meaning: a heathen worships false gods or images
a procrastinator might confess to putting things off by saying I do it later

explanation.surface: A pagan confesses to always putting things off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: a procrastinator's admission is I DO LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol-worshipper venerates images of false gods, which is what a heathen was taken to do; a putter-off says 'I do later'.

clue.text: Nonagenarian's first 21?

parts.note: 21 points to the clue at 21 across, a birthday, so this asks which birthday is the first one a person in their nineties celebrates

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asks about an elderly person's first entry in some list.
explanation.walkthrough: The 21 is a cross-reference to 21 across, BIRTHDAY; the first birthday as a nonagenarian is the one on which you turn ninety.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone becomes a nonagenarian on turning ninety, so their first birthday in that decade is the ordinal for ninety.

clue.text: It does not continue after midnight tonight

definitions.text: It does not continue after midnight tonight

parts.words: It does not continue after midnight tonight
parts.note: something that stops when the clock strikes twelve tonight is the current calendar day, which then gives way to tomorrow

explanation.surface: Some event or offer is announced as ending at midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a notice that a sale or show ends tonight; what really ends at midnight is the present day itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The present calendar day ends at midnight, when the date changes to tomorrow.

clue.text: Lady be on board in other words

parts.note: on board means aboard a ship, and SS is the abbreviation for a steamship
in other words is the meaning of i.e., the abbreviation of the Latin id est

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get aboard, put another way.
explanation.definitionFit: Bessie is a female first name, a pet form of Elizabeth, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Sly drone aggravated old painter

indicators.note: aggravated means made worse or stirred up, so the letters of these two words are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cunning bore annoys a painter of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aggravated' tells you to rearrange the letters of SLY DRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Joshua Reynolds was an eighteenth-century English portrait painter and first President of the Royal Academy.

clue.text: County girl established routine

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a way is a settled habit or custom, as in being set in one's ways

explanation.surface: A local girl settles into her usual routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Galway is a county on the west coast of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, in the province of Connacht.

clue.text: Three-quarters of learned people took lines from books

indicators.note: three-quarters of an eight-letter word means six of its letters, losing the last two

parts.note: the literati are well-read, educated people
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs on lines

explanation.surface: Most scholars copied out passages from books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three-quarters of' cuts LITERATI to LITERA; 'took' is a link word joining it to RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary means relating to books and written literature.

clue.text: Part of speech by a man using identical words

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech in grammar
Tim is a man's first name

explanation.surface: A man's portion of a speech is quoted word for word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbatim report repeats something exactly, in precisely the same wording as the original.

clue.text: Wheeled city seat

parts.note: Bath is a spa city in Somerset, England
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: A chair on wheels from a famous spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a Georgian spa city in south-west England; the wheeled chair for invalids was named after it, so the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath chair is a hooded wheelchair for invalids, first used in the spa city of Bath.

clue.text: Chester had real trouble with Irish statesman

parts.note: Deva was the Roman name for the English city of Chester

indicators.note: trouble means disorder, so the letters of real are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: A man from Chester fell out with an Irish politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges REAL to LERA; 'had' and 'with' are link words. Chester's Roman name was DEVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eamon de Valera was a leader of Irish independence, later Taoiseach and President of Ireland.

clue.text: PM leaving new department talked in a relaxed way

indicators.note: new says the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement once the named letters are taken away

explanation.surface: With the Prime Minister gone from a new ministry, people chatted easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM leaving' removes P and M from DEPARTMENT, and 'new' rearranges the remaining DEARTENT. 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister, but it is just the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chat idly or casually, a relaxed kind of talking.

clue.text: Book an exceptional quintet for the author

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so these letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: a quintet is five, and V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Reserve an outstanding group of five musicians for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' rearranges BOOK AN to NABOKO; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was a Russian-American novelist, best known for Lolita.

clue.text: The way Edwin included gold that had been put aside

indicators.note: included means taken in, so the gold piece goes inside the other two

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way or road
Ed is a short form of the name Edwin
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Edwin's road held a hoard of gold that had been hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts the gold inside. OR is the heraldic word for gold, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stored has been kept in reserve for later use, laid by for the future.

clue.text: Do record one in either end of hunstanton finding sea-mammal

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the pair of letters taken from the town's name
either end of picks the first and last letters of the town's name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is told to record a sea creature found at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either end of' gives H and N from HUNSTANTON, and 'in' puts I between them. Hunstanton is a seaside resort in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal related to whales.

clue.text: Delivery date

parts.note: delivery here is childbirth, so the date of delivery is the day a person is born, celebrated every year

explanation.surface: A courier's scheduled day for dropping off a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a parcel arriving; the delivery is of a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: The anniversary of the day a baby is delivered is the day on which that person was born.

clue.text: Have curtailed officer commanding destruction

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding

explanation.surface: A commanding officer's orders are cut short, causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts HAVE to HAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread destruction or chaos.

clue.text: Singular quantity of parchment from the dead sea?

definitions.text: Singular quantity of parchment from the dead sea?

parts.words: Singular quantity of parchment from the dead sea?
parts.note: the famous ancient manuscripts found by the Dead Sea are rolled parchments; the singular asks for just one of them

explanation.surface: An odd amount of writing material washes up from a lifeless sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dead Sea Scrolls are ancient Jewish manuscripts found near the Dead Sea; one of them, in the singular, is the answer. 'dead sea' looks merely descriptive.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled length of parchment is the singular of the Dead Sea Scrolls, the ancient manuscripts found at Qumran.

clue.text: Order, say getting on top of a Greek character

indicators.note: in a down answer, being on top of means sitting above, so these pieces come before the final letter

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: A Greek person gets the better of an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on top of' places EG above A in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Liberal member entered branch

indicators.note: entered means went into, so the member letter goes inside the Liberal abbreviation

parts.note: M is a short form for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: A Liberal MP joins a local branch of the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' puts M inside LIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a large branch of a tree.

clue.text: Fakir overlooked part of city

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A holy man missed some part of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' points to letters inside FAKIR OVERLOOKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirov is a Russian city on the Vyatka river, named after the Soviet official Sergei Kirov.

clue.text: One or two ladies

parts.note: Eliza and Beth are two women's first names
Eliza and Beth are two women's first names

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether there are one or two women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' means one lady: the full name is a single woman's name, yet it splits into two shorter women's names. 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth is a single woman's first name, as borne by two English queens.

clue.text: Officer became PM

definitions.meaning: an official who manages a royal or noble household or a town's finances
Neville ... was the British Prime Minister from 1937 to 1940

explanation.surface: An official rose to lead the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamberlain is a household or civic official, and Neville of that surname held the British premiership before Churchill.
